rv.q: Already, if you are interested in new rock musicals, it's good value at 45 bucks (less for students). You get your money's worth in energy alone.
LOKI – THE END OF THE WORLD TOUR is loud, weird, funny, emotionally resonant, and unapologetically ambitious.
See this show if there is any way to do so: you don't want to miss it.
Loki absolutely blazes through its 150-minute running time and director Heather Currie and her cast are firing on all cylinders.
Loki: The End of the World Tour is the kind of original musical that proves, yet again, how fiercely inventive Chicago storefront theatre can be when it fires on all cylinders.

The songs range from soaring power ballads to raucous ensemble numbers (including the opening banger, "Fire and Ice"). Aly Amidei's clever costume designs also give a contemporary twist to the gods. Odin looks like the head of a biker gang, Freya is a glittery-gold disco queen, and Sigyn is a pop princess in a white corseted baby-doll dress.

Together this trio provides the soundtrack for the show and skillfully accompanies each of the vocalists in their songs. The band’s professional musical contribution, along with every one of the extraordinarily talented singers, should consider cutting a cast album—they’re really that good!
Loki—The End of the World Tour is an ambitious and imaginative production embracing spectacle without losing sight of its emotional core.
